title: CLCON/1/2016 of Registrar Gurukul Kangri Vishwavidyalaya AND ANOTHER Vs Haribans Singh Chugh

paras.text:
CLCON No. 01 of 2016
U.C. Dhyani, J. Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Sr. Advocate
assisted by Ms. Monika Pant, Advocate for the
applicants /petitioners.
Learned Senior Counsel appearing on
behalf of the applicants / petitioners makes a
statement that he does not want to press the
present contempt petition.
In view of above statement, the contempt
petition is dismissed as 'not pressed'.

2
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Civil Contempt Petition No. 01 of 2015
Registrar, Gurukul Kangri
Vishwavidyalaya & another .......
Petitioners
 versus
Haribans Singh Chugh .......
 Respondent
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Sr. Advocate assisted by Ms. Monika
Pant, Advocate for the petitioner.
U.C. Dhyani, J.(Oral)

By means of present civil
contempt petition, the petitioners seek to
summon the opposite party and that the
opposite party should be punished for
committing contempt of this Hon'ble Court.
2) An order was passed by this Court
on 18.12.2015, while deciding writ petition
no. 3186 (M/S) of 2015, to the following
effect:
"In the above circumstances, keeping in
view the principle of law laid down by the
Apex Court in Election Commission of
India vs State Bank of India, A.I.R. 1995
S.C. 1078, and having considered
submissions of learned counsel for the
parties, this writ petition is summarily

3
disposed of with the direction to the
respondent no. 1 to decide the
representations dated 26.10.2015 /
25.11.2015, made by the petitioners, in the
matter. Till the disposal of said
representation the respondent no. 1 shall
not compel the employees of the petitioner
to perform the election duties."
3) It is the submission of learned
Senior Counsel for the petitioners that despite
such an order, the teaching faculty and
employees of Gurukul Kangri
Vishwavidyalaya were called for election
duty by the District Election Officer / District
Magistrate, Haridwar, which appears to be in
utter violation of the aforesaid order.
According to learned Senior Counsel for the
petitioners, the counting is to start on
05.01.2016, and again, the teaching faculty
and employees have been called upon to do
the counting work for the Panchayat
elections. Aggrieved against the same,
present civil contempt petition has been filed.
4) One of the objects of contempt
jurisprudence is to uphold the majesty of law
and to ensure the compliance of order of the
Court. A writ petition, being WPMS no. 10

4
of 2016, which has been filed on behalf of the
petitioners today, has been allowed at the
admission stage itself. It is reiterated that the
District Election Officer / District Magistrate,
Haridwar (opposite party) ought to have
obeyed the order dated 18.12.2015, passed by
this Court in Writ Petition no. 3186 (M/S) of
2015. Orders dated 22.12.2015 and
23.12.2015, passed by the opposite party are
in utter violation of the order passed by this
Court on 18.12.2015. Since, a fresh writ
petition, which has been filed on behalf of the
writ petitioners today, the same has been
allowed at the admission stage, therefore, the
Court does not think it necessary to issue
notice to the opposite party. At the same
time, this court is inclined to issue a warning
to the District Election Officer / District
Magistrate, Haridwar (opposite party) not to
flout the orders of the Court at his whims and
fancies.
5) With the direction as above, civil
contempt petition stands disposed of.
